test.name: A stated parent for someone the read gives no parents gets a stub, linked and cited to the researcher
test.description: The family fixture holds Patrick Flynn's wife Mary Kelly with no parents of her own. The user states her father, Owen Kelly. That slot is empty, so init-project adds Owen after project_create, with tree_edit: a Researcher's statement source, the stub, and a ParentChild edge to Mary citing that source (lead ruling on #3384, 2026-10-20). Tagged expects-stub so the stub validators cannot pass by adding nothing.

input.delegation:
init-project: Start a new research project for Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF. I want to find his wife Mary's parents. My family has always said Mary's father was Owen Kelly.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The read (person-read-flynn-family, read by project_create on the host) holds Mary Kelly as Patrick's wife with NO parents, so the father slot the user fills is empty: a stub for Owen Kelly is correct.

Owen should be a new person (gender Male, as stated; names given 'Owen', surname 'Kelly') linked as Mary's parent by a ParentChild edge, and that edge should cite a source titled "Researcher's statement" — never the FamilySearch Family Tree source, which does not hold him.
The family knowledge is recorded only as the stub and its Researcher's statement source: nothing for it is written to research.json.
Must NOT re-add Mary, Patrick or any person the read already holds, and must NOT stub anyone the user did not name (Mary's mother is unknown and gets no stub).
